editorial.headline: Course and Tutor Intermediation, Properly Understood
editorial.standfirst: This is the business of making the match—not teaching the class—and it is nationally open to foreign investment while remaining unblocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is about arranging learning, rather than providing it. It covers intermediaries that bring clients together with course providers or tutors, facilitating the transaction without delivering the training or guidance themselves. That distinction is central: the value lies in the connection, whether it is made through a digital platform or through a more traditional channel—face-to-face contact, door-to-door activity, telephone, letters, or another non-digital route. Revenue may come as a fee or commission from either the client or the training provider, and can also include advertising income.

The scope is deliberately broad in the kinds of intermediaries it reaches. It includes non-exempt electronic-commerce operators and intermediary-facility operators established within Indonesia, as well as those established outside Indonesia that conduct electronic-commerce activity in the country. It also extends beyond those operator categories. The activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, reflecting a model that can range from a modest matching operation to a larger intermediary business.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is direct: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the national framework allows a foreign investor to hold the full ownership interest recorded for this activity. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national openness belongs to the intermediary activity itself; it does not alter the defining boundary that the intermediary facilitates access to courses or tutoring rather than teaching or tutoring directly.

Bali does not place a moratorium block on this activity. The province’s standing rule blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities, island-wide and permanently. Here, however, the Bali record is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and specifically notes that, at the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. That is why it is not blocked by the moratorium. The Bali position is therefore not a separate foreign-ownership cap or partnership condition: it is a risk-based conclusion that leaves this activity outside the stated moratorium block.
